q: The quantum volume (IBM metric for quantum computer quality) combines the number of qubits and the circuit depth achievable with low error. A device with quantum volume V = 2^n can reliably execute circuits of:
opts: n qubits, depth n, with error below a threshold
All Clifford circuits on n qubits
exp: Quantum volume QV = 2^n means the device can reliably (with ≥ 2/3 heavy output probability) execute random square circuits of n qubits and depth n. It is a single number capturing the effective quality (combining T₂ time, gate fidelity, connectivity, and cross-talk). Doubling QV requires ~halving the error rate.
